principal_finding: The strongest Pilot-A organization is not persistence magnitude by itself, but compatibility of structural evolution across scale and time. D_STITCH is the only primary descendant that survives all three chamber views as organized: constrained in ROUTE-I, geometrically persistent in STRUC-I, and nearly globally connected in STRUC-PERC-I.

established_within_pilot: ROUTE-I constrained routing relative to the frozen degree-preserving route-null ensemble.
Enhanced temporal persistence relative to that null.
Very low real scale-time stitching defect relative to that null.
D_STITCH Geometric Persistence in STRUC-I, reproduced at 2,000 and 10,000 MC runs.
D_STITCH Giant Component Percolation in STRUC-PERC-I.
The [1,2,4,8] sensitivity run retains the ROUTE-I verdict.
supported_but_not_yet_generalized: Rare high-D_STITCH events are enriched in high-enstrophy / high-dissipation-proxy structures.
Scale-time compatibility appears more structurally privileged than persistence magnitudes.
open: Whether the D_STITCH signature generalizes to other spatial cutouts, time windows, Reynolds numbers, or turbulence classes.
Whether geometry-constrained or field-level nulls preserve the scale-time stitching contrast.
Whether high-D_STITCH events can be identified with a standard intermittency observable or event class.

next_research_question: Why is scale-time stitching organized when the persistence coordinates themselves are not?
